ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** All expected ideas are present with the correct topical identity: the dog-recognition opening, the single-modality-training distinction for AI systems, the researchers' two findings (cross-dataset/cross-architecture similarity; similarity increasing with capability) with citations, the Platonic representation hypothesis naming and follow-up-work citations, the Plato's Cave allegory and its AI adaptation, the Isola "shadows of the same world" quote, the methodological-contention framing, the "consensus unlikely" statement, and the "not bothered" Isola quote. One narrower point: the expected section's single-modality-training example includes two "exotic" illustrations (odor of molecules, protein structure) alongside text/image; the generated section keeps only the text/image example. The underlying idea (AI systems typically train on one data type) is still fully conveyed via the retained example, so this is not treated as a missing substantive idea, though a stricter reading could differ.

The Company Being Kept:
**1:** All core ideas are present with matching substance: Pythagoras's "All is number," representations as high-dimensional uninterpretable vectors, within-model similarity (dog close to pet/furry, far from molasses) via the Firth quote and the relational-neighborhood framing (mammal/animal/pet/furniture), the cross-model "similarity of similarities" technique with the Sucholutsky quote and the animal-word (dog/cat/jellyfish/wolf) example, the Anna Karenina scenario with the Tolstoy nod, and the vision-only-era limitation before large paired vision-language datasets existed. The generated section is if anything more explicit than the expected section on the vision-to-language transition point, which is an allowed addition, not an omission.

Convergent Evolution:
**1:** All core ideas are present: the early-2023/ChatGPT-era framing, the "existential life crisis" quote and the Isola/Cheung/Wang meetings, the increasing-strength hierarchy of convergence evidence (same data -> different data same modality -> cross-modal), the year-later decision to write the paper, and Huh's experiment (five vision models, 11 language models, captioned Wikipedia pictures, steady increase in similarity as models scale). One nuance: the expected section explains why same-data convergence is the weakest evidence (models could just be "grasping quirks of the training dataset") directly alongside the hierarchy; the generated section states the hierarchy without repeating that justification there, though the same memorization-vs-world-model tension is established in the section's own opening paragraph.

Find the Universals:
**1:** All core ideas are present: the catalog of experimental degrees of freedom (layers, similarity metrics -- the generated section names CKA and RSA explicitly, which the expected section does not do in visible prose -- and which representations/dataset to probe), the Wolfram generalizability quote, the Isola-vs-Efros contrast with quotes on both sides (including Efros's remark on Huh's Wikipedia dataset specifically), the practical-payoffs paragraph (translation, joint multimodal training, plus additional real-world application detail), and the closing Clune quote. One nuance: the expected section's Isola paragraph includes his acknowledgment that "the issue is far from settled" and that no one paper can resolve it; the generated section keeps the "seeks universals" quote and stance but not that specific acknowledgment.
